surfaces.name: Calyx macOS app (Swift, AppKit/SwiftUI, libghostty; macOS 26, Apple Silicon)
calyx CLI and calyx-session daemon CLI bundled in the app

claims.answer: macOS 26 Tahoe or later on Apple Silicon only (direct zip with Sparkle updates, or Homebrew cask); bundled calyx and calyx-session CLIs; no mobile, browser or editor clients; remote persistent sessions over SSH.

scope.version: release v0.50.1 (2026-10-23, commit 2dfb7a4); help docs commit 4e50d02; site commit 673e684
scope.plan: Open source (MIT) macOS app, free download; no paid plan

desktop_os.answer: README: requires macOS 26 Tahoe or later on Apple Silicon (arm64 only); release v0.50.1 ships one Calyx.zip; the Homebrew cask installs the same zip.

mobile_apps.answer: README, site and help center list only a macOS app; bounded search found no iOS or Android project (project.yml has a macOS target only).

browser.answer: No web client; the app embeds WKWebView browser tabs for browsing, not for controlling Calyx.

mobile_browser.answer: No web or mobile client exists.

cli.answer: `calyx` CLI (browser scripting, open tabs, install to PATH) and `calyx-session` daemon CLI.

editor_extensions.answer: No IDE extension; Calyx writes a pi extension into pi's own directory for integration.

task_actions.answer: Start agents in panes or worktree tasks, steer through terminal and compose overlay, approve from the approval panel, review diffs with line comments and resume agent conversations.

notifications.answer: macOS notifications for approvals and OSC 9/99/777 terminal notifications with unread badges.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Persistent and remote sessions let shells outlive the app and live on an SSH host, but the GUI is a single-Mac client.

limitations: Partly met or absent atomic parts: mobile_apps, browser, mobile_browser, editor_extensions, cross_device_continuity; see each atomic answer for the limitation.

claims.answer: Launches terminal agent CLIs in panes: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, Grok and pi, with hooks and an MCP server for integration; no embedded harness; any other CLI runs as a plain terminal program.

custom_adapters.answer: Any CLI runs in a terminal pane but only the six named agents get status, approval hooks and IPC configuration; no adapter API.

session_integration.answer: Calyx launches the agent CLI as the pane's process and integrates through hooks, config files, an MCP server and a pi extension rather than an API session.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Peers across different agents exchange messages through calyx-ipc and one approval inbox handles several agents.

limitations: Partly met or absent atomic parts: model_providers, custom_adapters; see each atomic answer for the limitation.

claims.answer: Calyx handles no model access; each agent CLI uses its own subscription or API login, so existing subscriptions work as the CLI supports them; no vendor credits and no account.
